sessions.title: Introduction: Why we read what we read?
sessions.description: In the first week, we will discuss our reading choices and what influences what we read in school or in our free time. We will also introduce the concepts of Canon and marginalization in Arabic literature.

materials.title: Treason Our Text: Feminist Challenges to the Literary Canon

activities.description: we will discuss our reading choices and what influences what we read in school or in our free time.

sessions.title: Latifa al-Zayyat: The dilemma of nationalism
sessions.description:
We are going to explore the world of Latifa al-Zayyat and discuss why her novel al-Bab al-Maftuh the Open Door was canonized. We will read less known works by her in order to understand her literary journey and complicated relationship with the Nasser regime.

Assignment: Write a 400 words reflection on the reading. Details will be posted accordingly.

activities.description: discuss why her novel al-Bab al-Maftuh the Open Door was canonized.

sessions.title: Fluri ‘Abd al-Malik: Romanticism in the sixties
sessions.description: What is romanticism, and how Arab women poets had influenced the Arabic romantic movement? We are going to introduce romanticism as a literary movement and the marginalization of women poets who belonged to the literary movement.

sessions.title: Women writing Elegies
sessions.description:
We are going to explore the classical Arabic tradition of elegies written by women in the pre-modern period. Al-Khansa, as a case study, will be demonstrated and read alongside the canonization of her work. We will question who and how she is mourning.

Assignment: Write a 400 words response on Fatma al-Muhsin's text. Details will be posted accordingly.

sessions.title: Modernity and Elegies
sessions.description: How do modern elegies differ from classical ones? Did how and who women mourn in their poems change from what we read in the previous week? This week we are going to read modern Arabic literature elegies by Fadwa Tuqan, Gamila al‘Alayili and Nazik al-Malaika.

materials.title: modern Arabic literature elegies
materials.note: Fadwa Tuqan, Gamila al‘Alayili and Nazik al-Malaika

sessions.title: Self-Writing
sessions.description: What genres do women write? We will discuss the literary genres of self-writing (autobiographies, diaries, letters…) and try to understand why they differ from novels and short stories. We will investigate how aesthetically different self-writing is from other plot-driven literary genres.

activities.description: We will discuss the literary genres of self-writing (autobiographies, diaries, letters…) and try to understand why they differ from novels and short stories.

sessions.title: Feminist Aesthetics
sessions.description:
Do women write differently? This week will focus on women's feminized literature and claimed literary genres. We will continue our discussion about self-writing aesthetics in an attempt to find common themes of women writing. We are going to mobilize feminist literary theory text by Anne Rosalind Jones.

Assignment: Ideas for the final project.

materials.title: Writing the Body: Toward an Understanding of l’écriture feminine

activities.description: We will continue our discussion about self-writing aesthetics in an attempt to find common themes of women writing.

sessions.title: Conclusions and Final Projects Presentations
sessions.description:
In our final discussion, we are going to survey what we read, wrote and concluded. Presentations are expected to illustrate individual projects about marginalized women authors. Students are encouraged to find unconventional texts such as orally transmitted texts, diaries and letters.

Assignment: 800 words paper on your final project. Details will be posted accordingly.

Presentations are expected to illustrate individual projects about marginalized women authors.
